title: The Name Tags in the Cloud Archive

segments.text: [soft, slow, warm voice] [quiet archive room ambience] [softly] Rest comfortably and imagine a quiet archive floating above the city, storing every label the mind has collected.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Let your name appear on a small glowing tag. Notice that the name is known. What is aware of knowing it?
[soft, slow, warm voice] Add another label: successful... awkward... tired... kind... too much... not enough. Watch the archive receive it.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Ask gently: am I the label, or am I also the space in which the label is read? No final answer is needed.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice a thought uploading itself. Then notice the tiny gap before the next thought arrives.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Feel an emotion as data in the body: warmth, pressure, movement. What notices the signal before naming it?
[soft, slow, warm voice] [thoughtfully] The archive is useful. Memory and identity help you navigate. Yet the present awareness cannot be fully compressed into a folder.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Let all labels float at once without selecting one as the final truth. Rest in the capacity to notice them.
[soft, slow, warm voice] If confusion appears, notice confusion. If spaciousness appears, notice spaciousness. Neither receives administrator privileges.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Return to the ordinary body, with its history, needs, and name. Inquiry can make identity lighter without deleting it.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Let the archive drift into the clouds. Open your eyes and return to the useful world of names.
